newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton extends gains on mill buying.
newsitem.headline: India cotton extends gains on mill buying.

text.p: Cotton prices extended gains on the local market on Tuesday as fresh mill buying dragged prices upwards with limited supplies aiding the firm tendency, dealers said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi moved up by 15/25 rupees at 1,000/1,075 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned rose by 15/35 rupees at 1,825/1,875 rupees per maund.
"Slow progress of monsoon particularly for the second round in producing centres also helped cotton prices bounce back after recent losses," one broker said.
"Earlier the progress of monsoon was satisfactory but now the second round has been delayed," he said.
The slow progress of the monsoon also arrested fresh offerings by the state-owned agencies.
In the Gujarat segment, Kalyan cotton climbed by 200 rupees at 14,200/14,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while Wagad cotton rose by 100 rupees at 13,000/13,100 rupees per candy.
